texts.value: Catalyzes the NADPH-dependent reduction of several pentoses, tetroses, trioses, alpha-dicarbonyl compounds and L-xylulose (PubMed:11882650, PubMed:19337691, PubMed:40737316). Can use both NAD and NADP as cosubstrate but shows higher activity with NADP (PubMed:11882650). Participates in the uronate cycle of glucose metabolism (PubMed:11882650). May play a role in the water absorption and cellular osmoregulation in the proximal renal tubules by producing xylitol, an osmolyte, thereby preventing osmolytic stress from occurring in the renal tubules (PubMed:11882650)

Competitively inhibited by butanoic acid, which binds to the enzyme-NADP(+) complex (PubMed:11882650). Inhibited by 4-methyl-[1,2,3]-thiadiazole-5-carboxylic acid benzyloxyamide (MTB) and 4-methylthiophene-2-carboxylic acid N-(2,3,3-trichloroacryloyl)-hydrazide (MTT) (PubMed:15906319)
